feat: build index.json for .well-known/agent-skills in release pipeline (#77)

* feat: build index.json for .well-known/agent-skills in release pipeline

Replaces the inline bash tar loop with a TypeScript build script that
produces both skill tarballs and a discovery index.json conforming to
the agent-skills discovery spec (RFC v0.2.0). Applies improvements
identified in code review of #66:

- Deterministic archives: zero timestamps/uid/gid so digests only change
  when content changes (requires GNU tar; falls back to BSD tar with a
  warning on macOS)
- Exclude patterns: .gitignore-style walk skips .DS_Store, .vscode, etc.
- Auto-detect skill-md vs archive: single-file skills emit type "skill-md"
  and copy SKILL.md directly instead of creating a tarball
- Relative URLs in index.json: portable across serving paths
- Validate both name and description frontmatter fields

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: add .well-known discovery section and GitHub Action migration note to README

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: simplify release build script using tar npm library

Replace shell-out to system tar/gzip binaries with the tar npm package.
Drops the custom file-walker, exclude-pattern matching, GNU tar detection,
and BSD tar fallback — none of which are needed in a clean CI checkout.
Determinism is preserved via portable: true and mtime: new Date(0).
Always emits type: "archive" for all skills, removing the isSingleFile
branch since the spec recommendation is not a hard requirement.
Renames release-please.yml to release.yml.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: scope supabase-plugin app token to the correct installation (#88)

The second `create-github-app-token` step minted a token for the
sb-community-agent-skills-releaser GitHub App, which is installed on
`supabase-community/supabase-plugin`, not on this repo. Without `owner`
and `repositories`, the action defaulted to looking up the installation
on the current repo and failed with 404, breaking the release job's
final step that dispatches the downstream sync workflow.

feat(supabase): add debugging workflows to the supabase skill (#112)

* feat(supabase-debugging): add Supabase debugging skill

Add a model-invoked `supabase-debugging` skill giving an evidence-first
methodology for diagnosing Supabase apps: reproduce → isolate the layer →
gather evidence (ClickHouse logs, advisors, metrics) → fix → verify.

Includes nine layer reference files (logs & evidence, RLS & access, Data
API/PostgREST, auth, database, connections & pooler, edge functions,
realtime, storage) distilled from the Supabase troubleshooting guides.
All log queries use current ClickHouse `logs` syntax rather than the
retired BigQuery `cross join unnest(metadata)` form.

Register the skill in release-please config/manifest (seeded 0.0.0) and add
it to the sanity-test skill allowlist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(supabase-debugging): use event_message for Postgres log detail

parsed.query and parsed.detail are almost always empty in the ClickHouse
logs; select event_message (the raw log line, always populated) instead,
and correct the postgres_logs key list to the fields actually present.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(supabase-debugging): make efficient log querying the core doctrine

Lead the logs guidance with narrow, source-specific querying over a short
window that widens deliberately — the wasteful all-source scan is the agent
failure mode this skill targets. Add log drains for recurring monitoring and
a note that missing log_attributes keys return empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(supabase-debugging): close coverage gaps from corpus review

Add the PostgREST or()-on-mutation 400 bug, Edge Function CORS/preflight
handling, the supabase-js returned-not-thrown error note, the wrong-key
(anon vs secret) server-side RLS trap, and the pre-0.11 pg_net timeout
signature.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(supabase-debugging): steer agents off guessing log_attributes keys

Behavioral eval showed agents fabricate plausible-but-empty log_attributes
keys instead of matching on event_message or discovering keys first. Make
that an explicit rule, since a guessed key silently returns '' and hides
the signal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(supabase-debugging): add behavioral eval suite

Add evals/supabase-debugging/evals.json (skill-creator format): 8 scenarios
across RLS, Data API, edge functions, realtime, pooler, and auth, plus the
narrow-query efficiency thesis and the optimization-vs-debugging boundary.
Lives outside skills/ so it is not shipped with the skill.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(supabase-debugging): sharpen efficient-logging guidance from o11y review

- Warn against ultra-recent (1-5 min) windows that scan unsettled data;
  recommend ~15 min floor.
- Give the cost rationale for avoiding select * (edge events ~40 fields).
- State explicitly the skill is on-demand; recurring streaming uses log drains.
- Reframe widening as anchor-based cross-source correlation, not a fresh scan.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(supabase-debugging): tighten prose per Elements of Style

Copyedit SKILL.md and all reference files for clarity and concision (active
voice, omit needless words, positive form, keep related words together,
emphatic words last). Prose-only: code blocks are byte-identical, technical
values and em dashes unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(supabase-debugging): state get_logs returns the last 24 hours

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(supabase): fold debugging workflows into the supabase skill

Move the debugging skill into the supabase skill as disclosed reference
(references/debugging/), reached from a new Debugging section in SKILL.md
and error/logs triggers in the description. Every install of the supabase
skill now includes debugging, with no separate install and no extra
always-loaded description.

Remove the standalone supabase-debugging skill (never released) from the
release config, manifest, and sanity test. Move the eval suite out to the
supabase/evals repo (removed here).

* refactor(supabase): route debugging to troubleshooting docs

Skill files are downloaded to the user's machine and cannot be kept up
to date, so embedded cause/fix content goes stale. Nearly every symptom
the debugging references covered already has a dedicated Supabase
troubleshooting guide that the team owns and updates continuously.

Replace the 9 per-layer reference files with a symptom-to-docs router in
index.md that maps each symptom to its layer, log source, and the
canonical troubleshooting guide (fetchable as Markdown, with search_docs
as fallback). Keep only what has no docs equivalent: the debugging loop,
the request-stack model, and the ClickHouse log-querying method in
logs-and-evidence.md.

* fix(supabase): correct logs guidance to the live BigQuery dialect

The public Logs Explorer runs on BigQuery (per-source tables,
cross join unnest(metadata)), not the ClickHouse model the log-querying
reference assumed; it even flagged the live syntax as "retired". Since a
skill file cannot be updated on users' machines mid-migration:

- Foreground the engine-agnostic MCP get_logs tool as the primary path.
- Keep the dialect-independent narrow-query discipline.
- Rewrite the minimal Logs Explorer examples in the live BigQuery dialect
  and label them, with a note that a ClickHouse migration is in progress
  and the docs are authoritative for current syntax.
- Drop the ClickHouse engine assertions from SKILL.md and index.md.

* fix(supabase): restore ClickHouse as the Logs Explorer default

The Logs Explorer now defaults to ClickHouse (single `logs` table,
`log_attributes` map); the public telemetry/logs docs page still shows
the legacy BigQuery syntax and lags reality. Put the log-querying
reference back on the ClickHouse model, keep MCP get_logs as the primary
engine-agnostic path, and note BigQuery as the legacy fallback for
un-migrated projects.

* refactor(supabase): delegate the ClickHouse log-query reference to docs

A troubleshooting guide now owns the Logs Explorer query method
(querying-logs-efficiently-in-the-logs-explorer, ClickHouse). To avoid
duplicating docs content, trim logs-and-evidence.md to the agent-specific
parts (the narrow-query discipline as behavior, the MCP get_logs/advisors/
schema tools) and link the query reference (logs table schema, log_attributes
keys, example queries) to that guide. Router now leads with it.

* refactor(supabase): link logs guidance to the Logs Explorer docs guide

The standalone troubleshooting page was folded into the existing
telemetry/logs guide, so point there instead. Since the live ClickHouse
dialect has no docs home yet (that guide still shows BigQuery), keep a
minimal ClickHouse query reference inline and note the translation.

* fix(supabase): correct request-stack model and log-query claims

From the PR audit: render the request stack as parallel services behind
the gateway rather than a linear chain (an auth failure does not pass
through PostgREST), note postgrest_logs is low-signal, complete the
get_logs to source mapping, soften the count() claim (ClickHouse accepts
count(*)), and hedge the ultra-recent-window explanation.

* refactor(supabase): route to the troubleshooting index, not per-guide links

Enumerating ~47 troubleshooting URLs in the skill duplicated the docs and
rotted on re-slug, on a file that can't be updated on users' machines.
Collapse the router to a stable symptom -> layer -> log-source map (no
guide URLs) and find the specific guide via search_docs or the
troubleshooting index; the docs Debugging guide is the overview. Same
treatment for the deeper-diagnostics list. One source of truth, in docs.

* refactor(supabase): link debugging docs as .md for lightweight fetches

The troubleshooting index now serves a markdown version at
/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md. Point the debugging skill's stable doc
links (troubleshooting index, Debugging guide, Logs Explorer guide) at
their .md variants so agents fetch the non-HTML-bloated page directly.

* refactor(supabase): drop debugging index.md, point to the docs guide

The debugging index duplicated the docs Debugging guide (the loop,
request-stack model, and symptom router now live at
/docs/guides/telemetry/debugging). Delete it and point SKILL.md and
logs-and-evidence.md at the docs guide, keeping only the agent-specific
log-querying method that has no docs equivalent.

* docs(supabase): tighten the Debugging section into a read-the-docs directive

Per review: reduce the inline explanation to a directive that points the
agent at the docs Debugging guide before diagnosing or fixing, and at
logs-and-evidence.md before querying logs.

* docs(supabase): state debugging intent with must, drop tool prescription

Per review: write the intent (the agent must consult Supabase's debugging
docs before diagnosing or fixing) rather than the how (search_docs/WebFetch);
let the agent pick the search mechanism its environment provides.

* refactor(supabase): reduce debugging to a docs link, drop reference files

The log-querying method moves into the Logging docs (ClickHouse + BigQuery
syntax). Delete references/debugging/ entirely; SKILL.md now points at the
Debugging and Logging guides as the single source.

* feat(supabase): add query_logs as a logs trigger keyword

* refactor(supabase): point debugging to the monitoring-and-debugging index

Docs restructured under /guides/monitoring-and-debugging with debugging,
logs, and advanced-log-filtering as subpages. Point the skill at the new
landing page instead of two hardcoded subpages, so future doc reshuffles
under that index don't require a skill update.

* docs(supabase): attribute errors to their layer, drop redundant sentence

Raw HTTP/Postgres error codes were listed side by side without saying
which service they came from. State the service/layer instead, and
drop the trailing sentence that just restated the must-fetch directive.

* docs(supabase): drop MCP tool names from the description trigger

Naming query_logs/get_logs in the skill description creates a hard
dependency on specific MCP tool names. Keep the trigger to
capability-level keywords instead.

* docs(supabase): note the debugging docs also cover performance

This reverts commit b9aaf157e28f2116e2b6b5cffebc3ae8f592105a.

fix(supabase): recommend scoped personal access tokens for the Management API, CLI, and MCP (#604)

The skill had no guidance on personal access tokens, so agents setting up
Management API scripts, CLI in CI, or the MCP server without OAuth tended to
suggest a classic token with full account access. Scoped personal access
tokens limit a token to chosen organizations, projects, and permissions.

Changes to skills/supabase/SKILL.md:

- Security checklist: prefer scoped personal access tokens for scripts, CI,
  and agents, and look up required permissions in the personal access tokens
  guide instead of guessing. No endpoint-to-permission mapping is copied into
  the skill, so it can't drift from the docs.
- CLI gotchas: the browser flow of `supabase login` creates a classic token.
  In CI, set SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN to a scoped token, which takes precedence
  over a saved login. Commands that connect with the database password (for
  example `supabase db push` with SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD) aren't limited by the
  token's permissions.
- MCP troubleshooting: where the browser OAuth flow can't run, pass a scoped
  token in the Authorization header. New step 4 explains the "You do not have
  permission to perform this action" error a scoped token returns when it
  lacks a tool's permission or the project is outside its scope.
